report_parsed.summary: The requested survey could not be executed as specified. Two hard tool limits were established empirically. (1) Metric resolution: every metrics query returned exactly one value per series at the end of its query window regardless of step (15 s, 300 s and 86400 s steps all produced a single point per series), and for the same series the value returned for a 900 s range selector over a 15-minute window was identical to full precision to the value returned for a 86400 s selector over the whole frame (119.9627705230877 in f7066412-9bc8-4f1c-a998-bd4049d9c220-t0:0062f7f9-72ab-4ff3-9de2-c99946e7f5f3 vs ec1dcb19-73c0-45be-876d-81e37713f0cf-t0:55a3b0f1-6cec-472d-acb1-1cd1a91b85ef). No 15-second-resolution error or latency series is therefore obtainable, and no latency/error trend can be computed or compared. (2) Trace volume: limit-50 searches over the 24 h frame were refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE for frontend (116114 tokens) and currency (62119 tokens), and even a limit-50 30-minute frontend search was refused (116113 tokens); trace evidence is consequently a small, explicitly incomplete sample (limit 2-5 over 10-30 minute slices), not a complete per-service trace census. Within those limits I obtained: whole-frame per-service span-count increases for 15 of the 17 authorized services (none returned for kafka or image-provider); whole-frame REST/gRPC counters; whole-frame p95 latency for four services; and 18 sampled traces across 6 services covering 15 service identities. No error-tagged span appeared in any sampled trace, and the only ERROR-tagged metric series (frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator, payment) each returned 0 over the frame; error status for the other services is unknown, not zero. Several distinct services returned bit-identical whole-frame values, which weakens per-service comparison of those counts. Conclusion is partial: useful per-service observations exist, but the complete 24 h x 15 s x 50-trace survey requested is not achievable with these tools, and no defect could be demonstrated or excluded.
